story_type: flooded neighborhood, airboats go house to house, Guard truck carries residents out
hook: The water was too deep for trucks. So the airboats went in.
narration: The water was too deep for trucks, so the rescue came by airboat.
This is Cocoa, Florida, on November twentieth, after severe flooding swamped whole neighborhoods.
Florida Army National Guard soldiers drove a high water truck in as far as it could go.
Past that, airboats went house to house.
An airboat has a flat bottom and a giant fan on top, so it can skim water only inches deep without a propeller to snag on cars or fences.
Crews helped residents off their porches and onto the boat.
Then the airboat ran them out to the waiting truck.
Soldiers pulled the door open and helped each person up into the cab.
outcome: The soldiers evacuated the residents out of the flooded streets of Cocoa.
